g.text: Scan and Re-scan - full transcription where the numbering has a hole
Between mismatched marks, and before the first
mark when it is not chapter 1 (or is below
--expected-start-chapter). The same mechanism
however the chapters were seeded - a --verify
recovery's confirmed marks are covered exactly
like a fresh run's own.
find the gaps in the chapter sequence
Scan
transcribe the region in chunks
match the missing numbers against it
Costs no audio: the chunk is decoded and its
transcript already in hand. What it may add is
bounded by the
same ledger
Probe answers to,
so the two passes cannot both claim one
announcement.
Scan produced no named mark at all until this
was added, and nothing had decided that: every
recovery path here is opened by a hole in the
chapter *numbering*, a named mark carries no
number and so sits in no hole, and the
blindness fell out of that. It cost most in the
trailing region - which is exactly where an
epilogue belongs.

A lighter upgrade model is the one unambiguous
statement that this file's stragglers are not
worth more time, and doubling the cost of the
gap it just failed on would be exactly the
opposite.
no re-scan
Re-scan
Not carried over from the loop above: a gap
Scan closed only in part has become one or
more narrower gaps around what it did find,
and those remainders - not the original
span - are what is left to read again.

Scan (trailing)
The one thing gap-finding structurally cannot
flag: nothing bounds a still-missing last
chapter from above to compare against. Two
independent things ask for it and both end
up here.
transcribe from the last mark to the end
a
targeted
sweep, and no downgrade?
yes
open-ended
a shifted re-read may follow
The open-ended scan runs on every file by
default, and a second reading of audio
nothing suspects would double that standing
cost for the whole library. It is not left
unprotected: snapping its own seams is what
keeps an announcement off a chunk border in
the first place.
one pass only, its own seams
snapped to silences
yes
a trailing region to read?
Why the shift works.
An announcement sitting on a
chunk boundary can vanish from the transcript
entirely while the timeline stays contiguous, so
the text reads as if nothing were missing. Half a
window is the displacement that moves whatever sat
on a boundary as far from one as it can get.
Shifting the region's
start
rather than re-planning
its chunks is what makes this cheap and hole-free:
the first attempt already covered every second, so
the head this skips is not unread, merely not
re-read.
Neither attempt snaps its seams where the other may
run - otherwise seam snapping could land a later
chunk back on its original border and hand the
re-read the framing that had already failed.
